scope: 15 whole exclusions, all fields inspected; each repeated scope field corrected. Exact integrated approval pending.
additional_source_basis: 396/398/402/404 fully reread in the prior 27-referral pass; all owned later pages previously received the lead pre-draft source-first pass and assigned current-record review.

rows.review_disposition: 304 treats Chateaubriand as an example of devotion despite limited personal obligation, and shows noble former officers serving in the ranks. Keep émigré motives and social composition; a separate memoir-writer unit is optional for this passage.

298/300 support cool foreign reception, fear of French reprisals and Louis XVI blocking the Lyon project. Retain these distinct diplomatic constraints under émigré plans; do not turn reluctance into uniform hostility or exclude the rulers’ independently developed treatment elsewhere.

313/314 explicitly connect creditors with delayed travel and Scottish refuge. This is more than decorative colour because it constrains Artois’s movements. Keep financial dependence as subordinate access within his leadership, while excluding a separately weighted debt biography.

323 uses Tone as witness to specie distrust; 325 also uses him on political theatre and 342 develops his Irish fate. The local monetary quotation creates no additional biography, but must not imply whole-book exclusion of Tone.

319/322/325 use anonymous testimony for economic hardship and political comparison. Preserve price/festival priorities, hunger and remembered Robespierrist protection as perceptions; do not endorse the claim that only the rich died under Robespierre.

320 supports Dreux as a catalyst in sectional coordination, including limited attendance and disagreement. No separate riot unit is needed; retain its trigger role and the broader causes of Vendémiaire.

341 develops a concrete strategic gamble: eight ships were removed while an Irish rising was known to be imminent. Preserve that vulnerability and Anglo-French strategic choice within the Irish expedition/naval context rather than discarding the argument with the personal decision.

341 supplies a Pembrokeshire landing but does not name Fishguard on this page. Use the source’s place wording in the exclusion. Keep the attempted British chouannerie and demonstrated weakness of maritime control under the expedition route.

342/351 support Hoche’s death affecting Irish planning and his proposed Cis-Rhenan state as rivalry with Bonaparte. Local nonduplication is acceptable; whole-book Hoche access remains substantive and cannot be made conditional on an expansive name policy.

347/352/367 use witnesses to establish Dutch impoverishment, Rhenish plunder and Italian radical hostility. Attribution alone is not a new personal subject, but the three regional mechanisms remain independently meaningful.

370/371 support exact personnel replacements and the apparent legislative victory concentrating power with Sieyès. Individual biography is optional; retain the constitutional pretext, threatened purge and reversal of legislature/executive power.

390 develops religious restoration as a political ending as well as ceremony. The preacher and decorations may be subordinate, but the public celebration, peace, restored worship and suppression of political conflict must retain access through the settlement/end-of-Revolution route.

391 contrasts British demonology with observed ordinary people and links Calais’s welcome to renewed ferry/tourist income. Exclude a separate Burney biography, not wartime travel restrictions, reopening or their economic consequences.

396/398 quotations support exile, lost subordination and clerical trauma; none by itself requires a biography. Keep the social and religious consequences, including the ability to support the Concordat despite antipathy to revolution.

402/404 use different local industries and ports to explain lost elite demand, blockaded colonial commerce and redirected land trade. Individual statistical microheadings are optional, but divergent local effects cannot be flattened into a uniform national decline.
